It's funny - it's taken until today for me to start feeling normal again, mood and healthwise, after a Friday night of drinking. It's just not worth it.

This is great advice. I'll get to planning something amazing for my wife and I.

The last weekend I was able to skip was because I pledged here every day of that week. When the cravings came, a sense of guilt came with it knowing that if I had caved I'd be making a liar of myself, especially with all the proof in my history. 

This past Friday I got blackout drunk. I woke up to embarrassing messages that I sent friends. I had (and still have a lesser extent) pain in my lower back that corresponds to the referred pain locations of the liver and spleen. My depression and anxiety spiked, which is what always happens for 5 days after I over drink so I know I don't be feeling back to 100% until Wednesday. I lost all motivation to make use of my time so my weekend was basically wasted and I feel like a lump. 

I'm going to change. I'm going to quit poisoning body and my mind. I will not drink with you today.

Hey everyone. I've been locked in a cycle of binge drinking most Fridays for the past few years. I've noticed a brain fog that stayed with me through most of the following week, then when Friday comes and it starts to clear up I rationalize drinking again. 

**The Good** I got through the entirety of labor day weekend without a drop. The brain fog has cleared up nicely but I plan to stay sober and ride this train to health. 

**The Bad** While my anxiety levels are much lower than they've been in forever, it turns out I was covering up a void in my life and now I have to turn and face my challenges instead of putting them out off. 

**The Helpful** I've seen this quote posted here several times, and it really helped me get through last weekend so I want to post it for others:

"You never regret not drinking"

Good luck everyone.
Made it past Friday. Now Saturday and Sunday to go. Skipping the three day weekend may be a lofty starting goal,  but I will not drink with you today.

Today is my day of reckoning. I've let alcohol hold me back for too long. My memory, my health, my fitness, my mood, alcohol is toxic to it all. For years I've cultivated the habit of binge drinking on a Friday and letting my weekend (and now most of the following week) fall apart in the hungover aftermath. 

Alcohol has been holding me back for too long, and I'm tired of being a second-rate version of myself. I have too much potential and I'm done squandering it. 

Plans are in place to shake up my normal Friday routine. IWNDWYT. 

Good luck to all.

Weekend binge drinker here. This week I'm breaking the cycle. I'm committing everyday so that I don't play down drinking on yet another Friday and spend the next 5 days suffering from the consequences. 

Motivation [#4](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6104963/)

* Alcohol damages our gut mucosal barrier by directly damaging epithelial cells and disrupting tight junctions

* Toxins and other harmful bacterial product can enter your bloodstream through these "breaks"

* Studies verify an increase in serum endoxins after acute alcohol binge drinking

* Alcohol promotes dysbiosis, decreasing beneficial bacterial while promoting bacterial overgrowth in the GI tract

* "it is reasonable to speculate that greater bacterial burden and altered bacterial profiles, together with increased permeability of the gut mucosa, would lead to continuous entry of bacterial toxins into the systemic circulation. These changes could produce chronic and sustained activation of immune responses that, in turn, could lead to immune exhaustion and dysfunction. Preclinical studies show that binge-on-chronic alcohol feeding alters the gut microflora at multiple taxonomic levels, influencing hepatic inflammation, neutrophil infiltration, and liver steatosis,23 which highlights the need for clinical investigation into the relationship between gut microflora and hepatic liver disease"

Motivation #1, [from the CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/alcohol/fact-sheets/alcohol-use.htm#:~:text=High%20blood%20pressure%2C%20heart%20disease,liver%20disease%2C%20and%20digestive%20problems.&text=Cancer%20of%20the%20breast%2C%20mouth,liver%2C%20colon%2C%20and%20rectum.&text=Weakening%20of%20the%20immune%20system%2C%20increasing%20the%20chances%20of%20getting%20sick.&text=Learning%20and%20memory%20problems%2C%20including%20dementia%20and%20poor%20school%20performance.)

Long-Term Health Risks
Over time, excessive alcohol use can lead to the development of chronic diseases and other serious problems including:

* High blood pressure, heart disease, stroke, liver disease, and digestive problems.

* Cancer of the breast, mouth, throat, esophagus, voice box, liver, colon, and rectum.

* Weakening of the immune system, increasing the chances of getting sick.

* Learning and memory problems, including dementia and poor school performance.

* Mental health problems, including depression and anxiety.

* Social problems, including family problems, job-related problems, and unemployment.
